football_evidence.question: Can California’s pass rush get to CJ Bailey?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward NC State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.3 of the 3.8 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When NC State has the ball (big plays through the air): NC State’s offense turns 10.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and California’s defense gives up explosive gains on 16.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When NC State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): NC State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 16.8% of its runs, and California’s defense stops 11.7% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
When NC State has the ball (third down): NC State’s offense converts 50.3% of its third downs, and California’s defense allows opponents to convert 40.7% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

Jackson Brousseau has completed 74 of 121 passes (61.2%) for 662 yards, 5.5 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and no interceptions in five games for California, and has been sacked on 4 of 125 dropbacks.
contradicting: When California has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): California’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.9% of its dropbacks, and NC State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 3.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When California has the ball (the red zone): California’s offense succeeds on 54.8% of its red-zone plays, and NC State’s defense allows success on 48.3% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).

When California has the ball (big plays on the ground): California’s offense turns 3.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and NC State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 11.0% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When NC State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): NC State’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.5% of its dropbacks, and California’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
quarterbacks: CJ Bailey has completed 141 of 221 passes (63.8%) for 1,738 yards, 7.9 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in seven games for NC State, and has been sacked on 11 of 232 dropbacks.

Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele has completed 148 of 217 passes (68.2%) for 1,575 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in seven games for California, and has been sacked on 10 of 227 dropbacks.
